seg_p0033_s0001: They were being crushed in the manner of fish and locusts, and like flies and gnats; for without knowledge of his Creator, every man is a beast. But now the passion of Christ and his resurrection resound in the voices and writings of all peoples.”
seg_p0033_s0002: For when the fullness of time had come, “the mystery which had been kept silent from the times of the ages was made manifest, and through the prophetic Scriptures, by the command of the eternal God, was declared to all peoples for the obedience of faith.” And from this that light, destined to be revealed to the peoples, shone upon those who were set in darkness and the shadow of death: concerning which God speaks through the prophet, “I have appointed you to be a light to the peoples, that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.” For when Christ commanded his apostles to go out into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature, they went out and preached everywhere, so that they allowed no place to remain hidden from the heavenly doctrine; “μὴ νήσους, μὴ ἤπειρον, μηδ' εἴτινα τρίτην ἀνθρώποις κατοικίαν ἡ φύσις ἐδίδου [neither the islands, nor the mainland, nor any third dwelling-place that nature had granted to humankind],” as Gregory of Nyssa puts it. And thus was fulfilled what God had once foretold through Isaiah: “I will send some of them to the peoples in the ocean, and to the most remote islands, which had not heard my fame nor seen my glory, that they may declare my glory among the peoples.” For “the word of God,” — these are Augustine’s words — “has been preached not on the continental land alone, but also in the islands, which are set in the midst of the sea: and these too are full of Christians, full of the servants of God. For the sea does not separate them from him who had made the sea.”
